# Decision history — legeos

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## legeos.constraint.identity-and-launch-safety

### Identity comes from the launch cgroup, never from a client's self-declared app_id; Exec= is never run through a shell; the governor is observe-only until traces are reviewed and never selects a victim by memory size alone

`superseded` · `@legeos.constraint.identity-and-launch-safety/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-appd/**"`, `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "services/lege-resourced/**"` · topic `identity-launch-governor-safety`

(1) A window's application identity is resolved PID -> cgroup -> instance -> canonical AppId; client claims (Wayland app_id, WM_CLASS, sandbox id) can only lower confidence (claim mismatch) or, when unique, yield claim-only confidence — never override a verified launch, and privileged actions require verified-launch. (2) Applications are launched as the registered executable plus an argument vector in a dedicated systemd unit; Exec= lines are parsed, never passed to a shell. (3) lege-resourced ships observe-only; enforcement (memory.high, reclaim, checkpoint, cgroup.kill) is enabled in stages after recorded traces are reviewed; the victim score weighs growth, PSI contribution, foreground/visible state, unsaved work and disposability, never resident size alone; session-critical units are never candidates.

**superseded by** `@legeos.constraint.identity-and-launch-safety/2`

## legeos.constraint.one-provider-per-role

### Exactly one selected provider per exclusive system role may autostart

`superseded` · `@legeos.constraint.one-provider-per-role/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-session-core/src/autostart.rs"`, `path "crates/lege-session-core/src/providers.rs"`, `path "crates/lege-types/src/provider.rs"` · topic `one-provider-per-role`

For every ProviderRole (network-status-ui, notification-server, file-chooser, file-manager, lock-screen, association-broker, clipboard-manager, power-manager, screenshot-service, input-method, portal-backend, greeter) installing a second provider never silently starts both; the user or distribution policy selects one and only that one autostarts.

**superseded by** `@legeos.constraint.one-provider-per-role/2`

## legeos.constraint.packaging-and-render-thread

### Every component is a Debian package (nothing under /usr/local or untracked in $HOME); lege-window carries no async runtime or D-Bus dependency

`superseded` · `@legeos.constraint.packaging-and-render-thread/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "debian/**"`, `path "tools/xtask/**"` · topic `packaging-and-render-thread`

All binaries, units, manifests and policy files are installed by Debian packages (cargo-deb now, the vendored source package later); development installs go through a local apt repository. The compositor-side lege-window crate must never depend on tokio, zbus, async-std or smol because it runs on the compositor render thread.

**superseded by** `@legeos.constraint.packaging-and-render-thread/2`

## legeos.constraint.services-not-indicators

### System behaviour belongs in services; tray icons, panels and applets are views

`superseded` · `@legeos.constraint.services-not-indicators/1` · scope `path "crates/lege-session-core/**"`, `path "services/**"`, `path "shell/**"` · topic `services-not-indicators`

No policy (timezone discovery, power decisions, autostart choices, association defaults, notification storage) is implemented in a shell surface or applet; each lives in a service crate/daemon with a D-Bus interface, and the shell only renders and forwards user choices.

**superseded by** `@legeos.constraint.services-not-indicators/2`

## legeos.decision.a-place-is-a-drawn-structure-not-a-richer-rectangle

### Revision 1 — A Place's rung is a drawn structure inside its allocation, not a box with more text in it

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.a-place-is-a-drawn-structure-not-a-richer-rectangle/1` · scope `path "crates/templar-field/**"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/src/garden.rs"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/src/surface/design.rs"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/src/surface/field_screen.rs"` · topic `homegarden-form`

The layout engine keeps allocating rectangles; what is drawn inside one is not a card. A Place renders the structure its own use has earned, and the whitespace inside its allocation is part of that form:

- development/research → a branch structure: the root, the descendants that actually mattered, drawn as a tree with the heavier branches weightier;
- media → a horizontal shelf;
- document-heavy work → a loose folio/stack;
- a plain folder → stays a plain simple form.

The visual grammar is five dimensions and no more: **position = memory, size = relevance, shape = mode of use, material = identity, colour = state**. Enough to be rich; few enough not to become decorative noise.

Scale differences are aggressive once blooms exist. A lightly relevant place is a line — `[ Downloads · 2 new ]` — while a context that has dominated several sessions may take about a quarter of the usable field and expose its actual branch or shelf structure. "Same rectangle with more text" is not a representation stage. The test is whether a person can glance at Home from two metres and see which places currently matter.

The field has garden zones without hard sections: no `Projects`/`Recent`/`System` headings, only weak spatial tendencies. New grown objects land in one broad open landing region so first growth is not scattered across the canvas; manually placed objects keep their coordinates forever; a grown object regrows near where it last landed.

The substrate stays very quiet: a slightly warmer, mineral off-white, no aggressive darkening or decoration. Material texture appears only on established Places, never on the field. State colour stays scarce — neutral almost everywhere, with amber/red/grey carrying genuinely exceptional meaning.

**Context.** Outside review of the Homegarden plan, 2026-09-08, brought by the user. The plan described Small/Wide/Large as progressively richer rectangles, which is the same failure the bottom bar had: more text in a bigger box is not a different representation. The reviewer's alternative keeps rectangular allocation for the layout engine — so `lege_field`'s ops, inverses and reflow are untouched — and changes only what is painted inside one. This also settles the geometry axis the earlier plan deferred: shape carries mode of use, so Wide-vs-Tall stops being a separate problem. The branch body already exists in a first form (`shell/lege-shell/src/garden.rs::branch_rows`, drawn by `paint_branches` at the Large rung), so this is the direction that work was already pointing; what is new is the shelf and folio forms, the landing region, the aggressive scale range and the quiet substrate.

**Consequences.** Not yet built. It supersedes nothing: `@legeos.decision.homegarden-activity-grown-places` keeps every rule about how a Place is earned, aged and positioned, and this record only governs what one looks like. The Wide-vs-Tall geometry axis that homegarden.md lists as deliberately absent is now answered by `shape = mode of use` rather than by a `Representation::for_span` rewrite. Needs: a mode classifier per context (development / media / documents / plain), a shelf and a folio renderer beside the existing branch renderer, a landing region in the tender, a wider stage range, and a substrate colour change in `design`. The blooms this depends on for the small end (`2 new`) are still unbuilt.

## legeos.decision.agplv3-own-code

### Revision 2 — D13/ADR-0013 — own code is AGPL-3.0-only; lege-comp stays GPL-3.0-only (§13 combination); Silvaview-rs relicensed identically

`active` · `@legeos.decision.agplv3-own-code/2` · scope `path "Cargo.toml"`, `path "LICENSE"`, `path "debian/copyright"`, `path "deny.toml"`, `path "docs/adr/0013-agplv3.md"`, `path "interfaces/wayland/**"`

Every first-party crate, interface, document and asset is AGPL-3.0-only (repository-wide LICENSE, workspace license field, deny.toml allow-list, Wayland <copyright> lines, cargo xtask copyright default, full text in DEP-5 debian/copyright because Ubuntu's common-licenses has no AGPL-3). compositor/lege-comp stays GPL-3.0-only for ADR-0012's reason; GPLv3 §13 and AGPLv3 §13 permit the combination with each part keeping its licence. Forks keep upstream licences. Silvaview-rs (the author's SequoiaView port, previously unlicensed) is relicensed AGPL-3.0-only so its pure squarify/colour/cushion modules can be lifted into crates/lege-treemap.

**Context.** The Home Field work lifts code from Silvaview-rs; the author chose to put both projects under AGPL-3.0 rather than keep LegeOS on MPL-2.0 (ADR-0008) and relicense only the lifted modules. One strong copyleft also removes ADR-0012's asymmetry of one crate under a stronger licence than the crates it links.

**Consequences.** cargo deny allows AGPL-3.0 for own code and MPL-2.0 for dependencies only; contributions accepted under AGPL-3.0-only, no CLA; network use must offer source (§13).

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.agplv3-own-code/1`

## legeos.decision.appearance-is-a-working-field-with-two-themes

### Revision 1 — Appearance: Home is a working field, not wallpaper; two themes (monotone, Temple) share one thin geometry; TempleOS is borrowed as a premise, not a palette

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.appearance-is-a-working-field-with-two-themes/1` · scope `path "apps/templar-settings/**"`, `path "crates/templar-session-core/src/settings.rs"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/src/surface/**"` · topic `appearance`

The shell offers two themes selected by a shell.appearance.theme setting, both built on the same structure: a light (or dark) ground that exists to carry information, wallpaper off by default; one-pixel rules and hairline borders instead of shadows, glass and cards, with padding measured in text lines; the information row as a single compact status line (clock, then only conditions that are true) in a semi-monospace face; typography (headings, rules, indentation) as the grouping device, borders reserved for containers (folders, trays, projects, window groups); objects useful where they are, the representation ladder reading as one document growing rather than a card opening a window. Monotone: a single accent hue and grey rules. Temple: a saturated cyan and a royal blue for structural lines, focus and links, with red, green, yellow and magenta only for semantic state; never the 16-colour VGA palette across the whole shell. Mechanically, surface/design.rs's constants become one of two token sets, including the window-group accent palette; the visual baseline renders once per theme. What LegeOS takes from TempleOS is the premise that the home screen is itself a working information environment rather than a backdrop for shortcuts, which is what the Home Field already is.

**Context.** The user on 2026-09-03 said they lean towards a monotone theme as one option and a TempleOS theme as another, and shared an analysis of TempleOS's visual grammar (white working field, thin blue/cyan geometry, text as structure, embedded live objects, commands and GUI as peers, density without crudeness) with the recommendation to adopt it as a design language for the Home Field rather than as a skin. Renaming (labels and the product's name) is a separate later step.

**Consequences.** Not implemented this pass. The window-group outline and tile edge use an accent that will be per-theme. Any new surface drawn now (group tiles, the search panel, the Files context menu) uses hairline edges and no shadows so it needs no redesign when the themes land. A work record follows when implementation is scheduled.

## legeos.decision.base-ubuntu-2604-kernel-70

### Revision 1 — D1/ADR-0007 — Base is Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 'resolute' with Ubuntu's linux-generic 7.0; mainline 7.2 only as a transaction candidate

`active` · `@legeos.decision.base-ubuntu-2604-kernel-70/1` · scope `path "distro/**"`

The base is Ubuntu 26.04 LTS ('resolute') declared once in distro/base.toml; the kernel is Ubuntu's linux-generic (7.0 GA, HWE later), version-locked with Canonical-signed prebuilt NVIDIA LRM modules (linux-modules-nvidia-<branch>-generic) and firmware by the legeos-kernel / legeos-nvidia-{open,proprietary} metapackages. Mainline 7.2 is never hand-installed; it is a candidate for lege-hostd's kernel/NVIDIA transaction path.

**Context.** Ubuntu 26.04 = resolute, kernel 7.0 (renumbered 6.20). The planning docs advise against placing upstream 7.2 on a hybrid Intel/NVIDIA laptop that already saw driver conflicts; reproducible driver validation and rollback matter more than kernel recency.

**Consequences.** One declarative base; NVIDIA via Ubuntu LRM (no DKMS, no .run installer); newer kernels only through the transactional path with the hardware matrix green.

## legeos.decision.boot-deploy-secure-boot

### Revision 2 — D5/ADR-0004 — Kernel/NVIDIA transactions on btrfs deployments with boot assessment and a system-scope health probe; bare metal boots through Canonical-signed shim + GRUB

`active` · `@legeos.decision.boot-deploy-secure-boot/2` · scope `path "distro/deploy/**"`, `path "distro/image/**"`, `path "services/templar-boot-health/**"`, `path "services/templar-hostd/src/deploy.rs"`

Root is btrfs subvolumes from the first mkosi repart layout; a deployment is a read-only snapshot plus a hostd-owned ESP directory (/EFI/legeos/<id>/) holding kernel, initrd and entry, so kernel + NVIDIA modules + userspace roll back together and Ubuntu's initramfs hooks cannot rewrite the previous entry. Kernels stay Ubuntu-signed Type #1 entries (no self-built UKI). A candidate boots with a boot-assessment counter; lege-boot-health (SYSTEM scope, before boot-complete.target, TimeoutStartSec + FailureAction=reboot-force) gates promotion. A BootManager trait has two backends: systemd-boot (bless-boot) and grub (GRUB_DEFAULT=saved + grub-reboot + hostd counter). RESOLVED 2026-09-03: the production bare-metal Secure Boot path for Developer Edition 0.1 is option (b), Canonical-signed shim → Canonical-signed GRUB → Ubuntu-signed kernel → Canonical-signed matching NVIDIA LRM, with hostd generating GRUB entries that carry legeos.deployment=<id> for the candidate and the known-good deployment. Dev/VM mkosi images keep systemd-boot with Secure Boot off. A LegeOS MOK (option a) is deferred until a self-built kernel exists; snapshot vs A/B for Stage 4 remains open.

**Context.** Ubuntu 26.04 ships systemd-boot but no Canonical-signed variant, so shim will not chain to it under Secure Boot without a MOK; a boot entry alone does not roll back NVIDIA userspace on a shared root. Option (b) gives real Secure Boot with no LegeOS signing infrastructure, which matches the first-release scope constraint and the Developer Edition 0.1 campaign's scope locks (docs/distroagentmidplan.md §2.3).

**Consequences.** The docs' watchdog sequence reuses systemd primitives; the deployment layout is fixed early; GRUB entry generation with the deployment id is implementation work under @legeos.work.reference-machine-provisioning and closes @legeos.question.grub-entries-must-carry-the-deployment-id; the mkosi image and the provisioned laptop use different boot managers by design.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.boot-deploy-secure-boot/1`

## legeos.decision.btrfs-delta-is-an-opt-in-catch-up-backend-not-the-default

### Revision 2 — The Btrfs metadata delta is the default catch-up for a downtime repair where the root is on btrfs and a checkpoint survives

`active` · `@legeos.decision.btrfs-delta-is-an-opt-in-catch-up-backend-not-the-default/2` · scope `path "crates/templar-file-index/src/btrfs_delta.rs"`, `path "distro/policy/polkit/org.templaros.host.policy"`, `path "interfaces/dbus/org.templaros.Host.IndexCheckpoint1.xml"`, `path "services/templar-filed/src/delta_catchup.rs"`, `path "services/templar-hostd/src/index_checkpoint.rs"` · topic `index-catch-up-backend`

`btrfs send --no-data` between two read-only `@home` checkpoints is the catch-up source for a **downtime repair** when the root's mount is btrfs and lege-filed still holds the checkpoint it left behind. Every other trigger — overflow, rename ambiguity, a policy change, a mount returning — reconciles as before: those are about what the index *believes*, not about a window of missed time, and replaying a difference does not fix them.

The three things the earlier revision held the default back for have landed. (1) Transport: `org.legeos.Host.IndexCheckpoint1.DeltaOpen(request_json s) -> (stream h, delta_json s)` — hostd writes the stream, opens it and unlinks it before returning, so the bytes reach exactly one caller and no path survives the call. Additive, so the frozen-signature rule is satisfied by re-freezing `interfaces/baseline.json`; the pattern is the one `Files.Index1.OpenSnapshot` already uses, and only the bus is new. (2) Disk cost: `Checkpoint.exclusive_bytes` from `btrfs filesystem du -s --raw`, serde-defaulted so the List JSON grows without a signature change, and `scripts/btrfs-index-fixture.sh measure` prints it with `filesystem usage` either side of the discard. (3) Cap: `DELTA_CAP_BYTES = 16 MiB` (`LEGE_FILED_DELTA_CAP_BYTES`), about 40,000 paths at the measured ~420 B/path — past which the measurements stop favouring the delta anyway, and the newer checkpoint is retained as the next baseline because the reconcile that follows brings the index current.

Polkit `org.legeos.host.index-checkpoint` moves to `allow_active=yes`, and it is the only action here that does: the caller is a daemon in the user's own session with no polkit agent, so nothing would ever answer a prompt and the repair would silently never happen. What is authorised is bounded to match — a read-only snapshot of the user's own `@home`, a metadata-only send, and a discard by an id that must be one safe path segment.

Every precondition that can fail is a `None` and a reconcile: not btrfs, no baseline yet, the baseline gone, the daemon unreachable, the stream over the cap, the decode or the apply failed. The recursive path is never removed, only skipped. On the ext4 development host every call returns `None` at the first check.

**Context.** The measurements were never the thing holding this back — `btrfs send --no-data` is flat within 4 ms across a hundredfold tree and about 24 µs per changed path, against a no-op reconcile of a 153,327-entry tree at 3.24 s that scales with the tree (@legeos.observation.delta-catch-up-cost-tracks-the-change-and-beats-a-crawl-except-on-bulk-creation, @legeos.observation.reconciliation-cost-tracks-tree-size-not-change-size), and the correctness gate passes field for field (@legeos.evidence.btrfs-delta-correctness-gate-passes). What held it back was three missing mechanisms, now built and unit-tested without needing btrfs, root or a system bus (@legeos.evidence.btrfs-delta-transport-and-backend-20260907). What has still never happened is a run on a real Btrfs root, a real `@home`, or across a reboot: everything measured so far is a loopback image on an ext4 host, up to 153k entries. That is why this revision is the default *for one trigger* rather than a general adoption, why every doubt falls back, and why the fixture gate stays a user gate in `RUNBOOK-L3.md`. One case is deliberately not taken: a directory that arrives from outside the indexed region is a single `Upsert`, because the stream names the directory and not the children that came with it. Rather than apply the delta and leave the subtree missing while the root claims to be current, that repair walks — which is also the one scenario the measurements liked least (the build-shaped burst, where a crawl won outright).

**Consequences.** A downtime repair on a btrfs `@home` costs what the change costs rather than what the tree costs, which on the reference machine's home is the difference between seconds and tens of seconds every time the daemon restarts. In exchange the system holds one read-only snapshot per subvolume between repairs, and a read-only snapshot pins every extent it references — user-visible as space that is not returned while the index is dormant. `Checkpoint.exclusive_bytes` is how much, and `Discard` is when it comes back; the number itself is NOT EXECUTED until the fixture is run. `lege-filed` gains a dependency on `lege-client` and reaches the system bus through `Handle::block_on` from the watcher's own thread — the route `lege_client::SyncSnapshotSource` already takes, so zbus's blocking API stays off. The ext4 development host and every nested session take the unchanged reconcile branch, so nothing about day-to-day work changes.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.btrfs-delta-is-an-opt-in-catch-up-backend-not-the-default/1`

**Consequences.** A downtime repair on a btrfs `@home` costs what the change costs rather than what the tree costs, which on the reference machine's home is the difference between seconds and tens of seconds every time the daemon restarts. In exchange the system holds one read-only snapshot per subvolume between repairs, and a read-only snapshot pins every extent it references — user-visible as space that is not returned while the index is dormant. `Checkpoint.exclusive_bytes` is how much, and `Discard` is when it comes back; the number itself is NOT EXECUTED until the fixture is run. `lege-filed` gains a dependency on `lege-client` and reaches the system bus through `Handle::block_on` from the watcher's own thread — the route `lege_client::SyncSnapshotSource` already takes, so zbus's blocking API stays off. The ext4 development host and every nested session take the unchanged reconcile branch, so nothing about day-to-day work changes.

**superseded by** `@legeos.decision.btrfs-delta-is-an-opt-in-catch-up-backend-not-the-default/2`

## legeos.decision.build-set-id-is-the-version-authority

### Revision 2 — The BuildSetId is the one version authority; debian/changelog is generated from it

`active` · `@legeos.decision.build-set-id-is-the-version-authority/2` · scope `path "crates/templar-build/**"`, `path "debian/**"`, `path "distro/apt/**"`, `path "tools/xtask/**"` · topic `package-version-authority`

The BuildSetId (<workspace version>~dev<epoch>+g<sha7>[.dirty], computed by cargo xtask build-set from Cargo.toml and git) is the single version authority for every shipped LegeOS package. cargo-deb receives it as --deb-version, and the debian/changelog head entry consumed by the source build is generated from the same value at build time rather than maintained by hand. os-release, distro/base.toml and the mkosi ImageVersion carry the product version (0.1) and are not package versions.

**Context.** The dev lane stamped packages with the BuildSetId while debian/changelog carried an independent hand-written 0.1.0~dev1, so a source build and a cargo-deb build could disagree (@legeos.question.package-version-authority-across-lanes). Chosen by the user on 2026-09-03 for the Developer Edition 0.1 campaign.

**Consequences.** One value flows to build-set identity, archive manifests, runtime stamps and the source package. A public release archive later needs a release grammar without the ~dev suffix; that is a revision of this decision, not a second authority.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.build-set-id-is-the-version-authority/1`

## legeos.decision.compositor-on-smithay

### Revision 1 — D12/ADR-0012 — lege-comp is built directly on Smithay, not forked from cosmic-comp; GPL-3.0-only is the one licence exception

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.compositor-on-smithay/1` · scope `path "compositor/**"`, `path "distro/forks/**"`

The compositor is written directly against Smithay 0.7 (MIT), with cosmic-comp read freely as a reference but no COSMIC crate in the dependency graph. It lives at compositor/lege-comp as a member of this workspace and is licensed GPL-3.0-only — the single licence exception in an otherwise MPL-2.0 repository, because cosmic-comp was read while writing it. cosmic-comp and cosmic-greeter are removed from distro/forks/manifest.toml; the greeter becomes lege-greeter over greetd's JSON IPC. The lock screen stays compositor-owned ext-session-lock-v1, which Smithay provides.

**Context.** Planning doc 01 §3 recommended forking cosmic-comp and deleting its window manager, judging that path "more likely to produce a usable system". That judgement predates crates/lege-window. Six measurements reversed it. (1) The layer a fork would keep is saturated with libcosmic: shell/element/ is 8,446 lines of which 7,304 (86%) import cosmic::/iced, so "keep element/, drop libcosmic" is not a cut that exists. (2) shell/focus/ is literally split-out `impl Shell` and `impl Common` blocks and cannot be kept while the thing it is an impl of is deleted. (3) grabs/moving.rs calls straight into the code a fork would delete. (4) Of 92 commits in the last 12 months touching the delete-paths, 52 (57%) touched a keep-path in the same commit, so the fork boundary would not insulate us. (5) input/'s keybinding model is an external COSMIC type. (6) cosmic-comp is GPL-3.0-only with no or-later clause. Meanwhile the largest part of any compositor — cosmic-comp/src/shell/'s 32,636 lines of window-management policy — already exists as crates/lege-window: 2,730 lines with no async runtime and no D-Bus. Smithay 0.7 already implements server-side every protocol LegeOS's documents name, including ext-session-lock-v1 and ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1, plus a complete XWayland window-manager role.

**Consequences.** One licence exception to track: debian/copyright carries a Files: compositor/lege-comp/* stanza and deny.toml allows GPL-3.0-only. Not in Smithay and ours to write: wlr-output-management, real screencopy capture, config, D-Bus glue and our two private protocols. Smithay is pinned to a git rev rather than a release, shared with cosmic-comp, which is a useful signal it works on this hardware. The winit backend is the crate's testable path where there is no display hardware, which makes it load-bearing rather than a debug aid: the protocol set is therefore constructed in one place (LegeCompState::new) so both backends provably advertise the same thing.

## legeos.decision.debian-packaging

### Revision 1 — D9/ADR-0009 — Packaging: cargo-deb per binary now; one vendored source package (root debian/) for the archive; keyring + pins as legeos-archive-keyring

`active` · `@legeos.decision.debian-packaging/1` · scope `path "debian/**"`, `path "distro/apt/**"`, `path "distro/metapackages/**"`, `path "packaging/**"`

Stage 1: every binary crate carries [package.metadata.deb]; `cargo deb -p <crate>` feeds a local aptly repo (never /usr/local). Stage 2: one source package `legeos` with debian/ at the repo root, vendor/ shipped in the orig tarball, dh_auto_build overridden with `cargo build --release --frozen --offline --workspace`; metapackages in legeos-meta; legeos-archive-keyring ships the archive key, deb822 legeos.sources and preferences.d pins rejecting third-party driver repositories. dh-cargo is not used.

**Context.** dh-cargo expects Debian-packaged crates — impractical for zbus 5 / tokio 1.5x / smithay; vendoring is what COSMIC's own packaging does.

**Consequences.** Packages from day one; the archive path is ready when the repository exists.

## legeos.decision.decorative-client-claim-icons-20261005

### Revision 2 — Unverified application claims are decorative icon keys only

`active` · `@legeos.decision.decorative-client-claim-icons-20261005/2` · scope `path "compositor/templar-comp/src/protocols_shell.rs"`, `path "interfaces/wayland/templar-shell-v1.xml"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/**"` · topic `decorative-client-claim-icons`

Expose a bounded decorative claimed_app_id separately from canonical AppIdentity. The shell may resolve it only as an icon key and must mark the resulting icon unverified. It must not use the claim for grouping unknown windows, grants, launching, MRU or Homegarden verified-instance identity. Unknown windows remain keyed independently by their WindowId.

**Context.** Unregistered clients can still supply a useful icon key, but the accepted identity/launch safety boundary forbids upgrading a self-declared application ID into canonical authority.

**Consequences.** Unknown clients gain recognizable display-only icons without claiming another application's rights or trusted task membership. Verified identity continues to take precedence.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.decorative-client-claim-icons-20261005/1`

## legeos.decision.event-driven-service-authorities

### Revision 1 — Local state has one authoritative owner with recoverable state-and-event delivery

`active` · `@legeos.decision.event-driven-service-authorities/1` · scope `path "crates/**"`, `path "distro/**"`, `path "interfaces/**"`, `path "services/**"` · topic `service-observation-and-activation`

Each local state domain has one authoritative owner. Consumers read typed state, synchronize a subscription without a read/subscribe race, and recover missed history by sequence or by taking a fresh snapshot. A generation identifies a committed view; an event sequence identifies change-log position. SnapshotRequired means continuity is unavailable and the consumer must resnapshot. Consumers never read an owner's private SQLite representation. Services use event or threshold wakeups and socket/D-Bus activation where practical; timers remain explicit for temporal conditions, backoff, bounded active episodes and reconciliation.

**Context.** Files.Index1 already provides sealed snapshots, ChangesSince(sequence), SnapshotRequired and freshness signals, and the filed watcher blocks with an explicit waker. resourced still samples and sleeps, so its conversion requires policy-preserving investigation rather than a blanket timer removal.

**Consequences.** Keep explicit browsing and narrowly documented service-unavailable fallbacks. Do not introduce a universal event daemon, RAM-only index, competing background crawlers, or a rule that every service must exit when idle. Each persistent daemon and polling exception records its authority, lifetime, activation, recovery, deadline and justification.

## legeos.decision.flatpak-and-crash-handling

### Revision 1 — D11/ADR-0011 — Flatpak for sandboxed apps (no snapd in the seeds); telemetry-free crash handling via systemd-coredump ingested into history

`active` · `@legeos.decision.flatpak-and-crash-handling/1` · scope `path "distro/policy/coredump/**"`, `path "distro/seeds/**"`

Sandboxed applications come as Flatpak (the alias model carries Flatpak IDs); snapd is excluded from the seeds and legeos-desktop conflicts with it. Crash handling: systemd-coredump on, apport/whoopsie out; lege-sessiond ingests coredump journal entries (PID -> cgroup -> instance) into the event history so a crash is one explainable, restorable event.

**Context.** Ubuntu forces the snap decision (Firefox/Thunderbird are snaps); the docs forbid 'a complete alternative application store' — Flatpak/Flathub is not that; the docs want notifications and system decisions as searchable history.

**Consequences.** One sandbox format in the identity model; crashes are attributed to instances without any upload.

## legeos.decision.forks-by-manifest

### Revision 4 — D6/ADR-0005 — External compatibility components are pinned forks; lege-files is a first-party service client

`active` · `@legeos.decision.forks-by-manifest/4` · scope `path "apps/templar-files/**"`, `path "distro/forks/**"`

Each remaining external fork lives in its own repository with an 'upstream' tracking branch and a 'legeos' patch branch; distro/forks/manifest.toml pins URL/branch/commit and `just forks-fetch` clones it into the gitignored forks/ directory. The standalone `lege-files` manager is instead a first-party Pixelkit application in this workspace: it depends on lege-client, owns no filesystem policy, and delegates browse, volume, operation, recents, search, path-action, association and launch decisions to the corresponding LegeOS services. This correction is required because the declared legeos/cosmic-files fork was never materialized and its configured remote does not exist; keeping the client local also makes the installable manager and its exact service contracts testable in the main workspace.

**Context.** The user's four separately maintained COSMIC submodules already caused rebase and detached-HEAD problems; Stage 2 wants proper downstream repos with automated rebase checks. The manifest model itself is unchanged by ADR-0012 — what changed is its membership: cosmic-comp and cosmic-greeter are no longer forks at all, so compositor/** leaves this record's scope. One of the six measurements behind that decision was specifically about this model's limits: of 92 cosmic-comp commits in the last 12 months touching the paths a fork would delete, 52 touched a kept path in the same commit, so the fork boundary would not have insulated us and the monthly rebase cadence below would have landed in deleted code constantly.

**Consequences.** No submodule state in this repository; reproducible builds from the manifest; monthly rebase cadence for the forks that remain. The compositor is now first-party (compositor/lege-comp) and carries no rebase burden; compositor/lege-comp-integration is an ordinary workspace crate rather than a path crate a fork depends on.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.forks-by-manifest/3`

## legeos.decision.home-field-default-leaves-slack

### Revision 1 — The Home Field's default leaves slack: floors below preferred sizes, and a drawer block bounded by a share of the width

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.home-field-default-leaves-slack/1` · scope `path "crates/templar-field/**"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/**"` · topic `density`

The default Home Field leaves slack rather than packing every tile at its floor. Drawer tiles take a 1x1 floor beneath their 2x2 preferred size and system tiles a 2x1 floor beneath their 3x2, so a resize has neighbours that can yield. The drawer block's shape is derived from the field's height instead of being fixed at two columns, and falls back to 1x1 shortcuts when a 2x2 block would claim more than a third of the field's width. All eight drawers stay on the field: the slack comes from lower floors, not from a shorter list.

**Context.** Asked as @legeos.question.home-field-default-density and left to the user: with floor and preferred both at 2x2 every neighbour of a resize was already at minimum, the clamp-rather-than-evict rule reduced every grow request to nothing, and the widget foundations' headline gesture did nothing visible on the default layout. Adding notifications as a third system widget settled it by making the old density unsatisfiable. Three system tiles at the 3x2 class floor plus eight drawers at 2x2 leave a 1200x800 field with no arrangement that both places the launcher and keeps every open window visible, and the project treats each of those as a defect: a window that is not on Home cannot be reached, and the launcher is the only route to an application with no window yet.

**Consequences.** The resize gesture does something visible on a field nobody has rearranged yet. A busy field degrades by compacting its furniture instead of failing to place it, so the launcher is always present even when every cell is spoken for. A roomy field looks as it did: 2x2 drawers still fit the width share at 1080p and above, and only a short or narrow field sees the 1x1 rail. The cost is that the default field is less information-dense than the drawers-at-2x2 arrangement on small screens, and that tile sizes now vary with the field's shape, which makes the layout harder to describe in a fixed diagram. The levers are DRAWER_WIDTH_SHARE and the two SpanRange floors in shell/lege-shell/src/field_model.rs.

## legeos.decision.home-field-stable-bounded-semantic-grammar

### Revision 1 — Home uses stable bounded rectangles, local reflow and explicit reversible semantics

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.home-field-stable-bounded-semantic-grammar/1` · scope `path "apps/templar-files/**"`, `path "crates/templar-field/**"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/**"` · topic `home-field-layout-and-interaction-grammar`

Home is a bounded field of stable rectangular objects. Moving or resizing one object triggers deterministic local reflow around the user's chosen anchor; content changes never move tiles, global repacking never destroys spatial memory, proximity never creates hidden relations, and Home does not become an infinite canvas or a set of disguised virtual desktops. A shape-and-area representation ladder controls information density while identity remains visible. Treemap layout belongs inside storage views, not across Home.

**Context.** The explicit semantic grammar is type-directed: file and folder references enter containers without moving the underlying item; app-on-app creates an explicit app group; project, window and widget relations are created only by named operations. Throwing, previews and richer widget execution remain staged features.

**Consequences.** Every destructive-looking gesture previews the outcome and offers undo or a keyboard-accessible equivalent. Preserve non-destructive references, containment, minimum usable sizes, stable type identity and bounded resource use. Reject arbitrary miniature full applications, ballistic deletion, content-driven reflow and proximity semantics. 'Content-driven' means index and content events (a folder gaining files, a drive gaining space, a widget refreshing): those never move, size, add or remove a tile. The user's own aggregated actions on a path (opening it, launching into it, editing under it, returning to it) are not content: under @legeos.decision.homegarden-activity-grown-places they may add, grow, shrink or remove a garden-owned Folder tile at a tending moment, never move one, and never touch a tile the user placed, moved, resized or pinned. (Revised 2026-09-08.)

## legeos.decision.home-is-momentary-and-placeable-objects-are-containers

### Revision 2 — Home is momentary chrome; folders, shortcut panes and widgets are placeable, loose files are not

`active` · `@legeos.decision.home-is-momentary-and-placeable-objects-are-containers/2` · scope `path "apps/templar-files/**"`, `path "compositor/templar-comp/**"`, `path "crates/templar-field/**"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/**"`

Home remains a taskbar-free surface rather than persistent desktop chrome. A short bare-Super press toggles or latches Home; pressing Super reveals Home immediately, holding it keeps Home visible, and releasing after a hold returns to the prior application view. Super chords remain accelerators and must not accidentally latch Home. Configurable Home panels, rails or docks exist only on Home and reserve no work area while an application is visible, so one application can occupy the entire output with nothing else shown.

The directly placeable Home objects are folders, composite shortcut panes/trays, widgets, projects and live/parked application sessions. An individual file is never a loose Home tile. Files remain immediately visible, selectable, previewable and actionable inside a folder or shortcut pane. A shortcut pane may reference files and folders from several directory locations without moving them; adding a file to such a pane adds a reference. The user's Desktop directory is represented by a default folder/shortcut pane on the larger Home surface rather than recreated as scattered desktop icons.

Object kind remains encoded inside a stable rectangular tile. Light colour, tint and optional material texture (for example glass-, stone- or paper-like treatments) may distinguish folders, shortcut panes, widgets and sessions, but geometry and interaction do not depend on decoration and themes own the exact material palette. Existing serialized loose-file tile data must migrate or remain readable, while new UI paths stop creating it.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.home-is-momentary-and-placeable-objects-are-containers/1`

## legeos.decision.home-projects-and-tool-actions

### Revision 2 — Home stores project intent; the FileManager provider opens folders; the taskbar selects running windows

`active` · `@legeos.decision.home-projects-and-tool-actions/2` · scope `path "apps/templar-files/**"`, `path "crates/templar-field/**"`, `path "interfaces/dbus/org.templaros.Projects1.xml"`, `path "services/templar-sessiond/**"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/**"` · topic `home-project-and-window-responsibilities`

Home is bounded persistent working memory for stable folders, collections, projects, widgets and explicit project/session relationships. Opening a folder launches whichever application holds the FileManager provider role at that folder (pcmanfm-qt by default since 2026-09-07, @legeos.decision.pcmanfm-qt-is-the-file-manager). The persistent bottom bar owns ordinary automatic per-window selection; automatic parked-window shelves migrate without losing explicit group, park or restoration relationships. Enter Project selects context and launches nothing, Launch Tool opens a provider-resolved role at the real project root, and Restore Workspace restores remembered applications and supported checkpoints.

**Context.** The filed service boundary (Browse1, Operations1, Trash1, Actions1) remains authoritative for LegeOS's own surfaces; direct mutation that bypasses LegeOS operation semantics from Home is rejected. The original 2026-09-07 draft named native lege-files as the folder window and rejected PCManFM-Qt; the user reversed that the same day on the installed session ("Files is too rudimentary to be used for now"), so the folder-window sentence now names the provider role rather than an application. Apps remains the remembered session application set; Terminal, FileManager and CodeEditor are derived provider roles rather than copied paths in every manifest.

**Consequences.** Projects1.Create receives the selected directory's real root; creation and pinning to Home stay distinct. Keep Apps launcher search separate from scoped Files search. Status updates never move tiles. Repository discovery never runs commands or hooks; build, test, run and repository status remain opt-in service work.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.home-projects-and-tool-actions/1`

### Revision 1 — Home stores project intent; the FileManager provider opens folders; the taskbar selects running windows

`superseded` · `@legeos.decision.home-projects-and-tool-actions/1` · scope `path "apps/lege-files/**"`, `path "crates/lege-field/**"`, `path "interfaces/dbus/org.legeos.Projects1.xml"`, `path "services/lege-sessiond/**"`, `path "shell/lege-shell/**"` · topic `home-project-and-window-responsibilities`

Home is bounded persistent working memory for stable folders, collections, projects, widgets and explicit project/session relationships. Opening a folder launches whichever application holds the FileManager provider role at that folder (pcmanfm-qt by default since 2026-09-07, @legeos.decision.pcmanfm-qt-is-the-file-manager). The persistent bottom bar owns ordinary automatic per-window selection; automatic parked-window shelves migrate without losing explicit group, park or restoration relationships. Enter Project selects context and launches nothing, Launch Tool opens a provider-resolved role at the real project root, and Restore Workspace restores remembered applications and supported checkpoints.

**Context.** The filed service boundary (Browse1, Operations1, Trash1, Actions1) remains authoritative for LegeOS's own surfaces; direct mutation that bypasses LegeOS operation semantics from Home is rejected. The original 2026-09-07 draft named native lege-files as the folder window and rejected PCManFM-Qt; the user reversed that the same day on the installed session ("Files is too rudimentary to be used for now"), so the folder-window sentence now names the provider role rather than an application. Apps remains the remembered session application set; Terminal, FileManager and CodeEditor are derived provider roles rather than copied paths in every manifest.

**Consequences.** Projects1.Create receives the selected directory's real root; creation and pinning to Home stay distinct. Keep Apps launcher search separate from scoped Files search. Status updates never move tiles. Repository discovery never runs commands or hooks; build, test, run and repository status remain opt-in service work.

**superseded by** `@legeos.decision.home-projects-and-tool-actions/2`

## legeos.decision.home-surface-visible-unless-covered

### Revision 2 — The Home surface is visible unless a fullscreen or maximized window covers its output

`active` · `@legeos.decision.home-surface-visible-unless-covered/2` · scope `path "compositor/**"`, `path "crates/templar-window/**"` · topic `home-visibility`

`Layer::HomeSurface` is the bottom layer and is visible by default. `WindowService::is_visible` hides it only when a visible, unshelved client window (`Layer::Normal`/`Layer::AppOnTop`) that is `fullscreen` or `maximized` resolves to the same output as Home (`WindowService::home_is_covered`, using `geometry::choose_target_output` on both rectangles, because a `WindowRecord` carries no output); a `reveal_home` reveal shows Home regardless and keeps hiding client windows exactly as before.

**Context.** On 2026-09-07 the installed session logged in to a black screen: `is_visible` returned `home_revealed` for `Layer::HomeSurface`, a fresh login has no reveal, so `space_sync` unmapped the Home surface from `Space` and the user had to press Super to see a desktop at all. The user's rule, verbatim: "i only want it to hide when there is a full screen window".

**Consequences.** A translucent client window now blends with the Home Field rather than with the clear colour — the previous rule existed for that reason and this decision overrides it. Home is mapped in `Space` whenever nothing covers it, so it takes pointer input on the empty desktop; it is the bottom of `stacking_order`, so a click over any window still reaches that window. A maximized window on a second output no longer blanks the first output's Home. No compositor code changed: `sync_after_change` already runs on every map, maximize, fullscreen, shelve, destroy and output-topology route.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.home-surface-visible-unless-covered/1`

## legeos.decision.homegarden-activity-grown-places

### Revision 2 — Homegarden: Home is a field of Places grown from the user's own actions, aged in session time, positioned by memory

`active` · `@legeos.decision.homegarden-activity-grown-places/2` · scope `path "crates/templar-field/**"`, `path "crates/templar-session-core/**"`, `path "interfaces/dbus/org.templaros.HomeGarden1.xml"`, `path "services/templar-sessiond/**"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/**"` · topic `homegarden`

Home deals with the user's stuff; the bar deals with the machine. Directories appear on Home as Folder tiles (Places) because the user opened, launched into, edited under or returned to them; they grow when activity concentrates there, hold their place while used, shrink and finally leave when neglected, and regrow where they were. A tile may change size, appear or disappear because of the user's aggregated actions on its path; it may never change position because of them; and it may never move, shrink or displace a tile the user placed, moved, resized or pinned. Tending happens only at tending moments (Home reveal, session start, an explicit garden.tend) and never while the user is looking. The tender emits Place, Resize and Remove only, every op with a reason, applied as one undoable batch. Time is Garden time: sessions counted and unlocked-session runtime accumulated at session start/unlock/lock/sleep/logout edges, never wall-clock; a machine that is off ages nothing. Relevance is evidence x recency-in-garden-time x breadth: a place used across several sessions with several roles outranks one burst of saves; machine churn (build output, caches, hidden dirs) never counts. Content changes may alter what an already-earned Place shows but never create one. Every visual variable has one job: shape = mode, material = identity, colour = state, size = relevance, position = memory. No context is ever turned into a Project by the system; no group is ever inferred.

**Context.** docs/garden/garden.md (the user's correction: no assumed main project, no fabricated first boot, no widgets that could be menus, closer integration with the file system, an organic system that notices where you work and tends it), docs/garden/homegarden-activity-grown-home.md (the model), docs/garden/garden2.md (session time instead of days, growth forms, branches vs blooms). @legeos.assessment.home-vision-review-20260905 left the mostly-empty cold Home unresolved; this is the answer: the emptiness is read, not filled.

**Consequences.** Revises the consequences of @legeos.decision.home-field-stable-bounded-semantic-grammar: 'content-driven' means index/content events; user-action-driven size change at tending moments is admitted. Supersedes the 'repack on activity' clause of @legeos.work.home-developer-setup-preview with 'resize in place at tending moments'. Phases 0-3 (ledger, Garden Clock, planner, tending at reveal, rung-aware Folder tile with roles row and branch body) are built first; growth forms/facets, blooms, material identity, sibling groups and a Wide-vs-Tall geometry axis are deferred until Phase 4 (a day's hands-on) judges the model. Wall-clock never appears in the garden's ageing; the Garden Clock needs session edges from Lifecycle1.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.homegarden-activity-grown-places/1`

## legeos.decision.independent-storage-roles

### Revision 2 — Provisioning declares independent storage roles and per-partition preservation policy

`active` · `@legeos.decision.independent-storage-roles/2` · scope `path "distro/deploy/**"`, `path "installer/**"`, `path "services/templar-filed/**"`, `path "services/templar-sessiond/**"` · topic `developer-edition-storage-layout`

One versioned layout contract describes device and filesystem identity, mount and subvolume roles, per-partition create/reuse/format policy, boot and deployment identity, recovery ownership, search visibility, acquisition coverage and accounting policy. Discovery and preparation are separate from deployment but use the same backend operation model. Dry-run and apply consume the same reviewed operation sequence, and apply revalidates topology, identity and mounted state immediately before mutation.

**Context.** The current existing-partition mode preserves the partition table but rewrites GPT type codes and formats both ESP and root. It is not preservation. The current root=LABEL=legeos-root boot contract also makes identity migration a coordinated provisioner, fstab, boot-entry and rollback change.

**Consequences.** Keep image, erase-disk, free-tail and existing-partition modes, adding explicit preservation semantics. No type-code rewrite or formatting occurs in preservation mode unless selected. A second data filesystem is optional and never assumed expendable. Preserve current OS subvolumes; stage optional @build and independent project/data/media/archive roles. Search, acquisition and accounting scopes are distinct; checkpoint activation remains opt-in and per filesystem.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.independent-storage-roles/1`

## legeos.decision.inotify-remains-the-index-event-backend

### Revision 1 — inotify stays the index's event backend; fanotify ships behind EventSource as a measured, unadopted alternative

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.inotify-remains-the-index-event-backend/1` · scope `path "crates/templar-fanotify/**"`, `path "crates/templar-file-index/src/watch.rs"`, `path "services/templar-filed/**"` · topic `index-event-backend`

InotifySource remains the default and only wired event backend for the file index. crates/lege-fanotify ships a FanotifySource behind lege_file_index::watch::EventSource so the comparison can be re-run, but nothing in lege-filed constructs it and no service links it. The privileged FAN_MARK_FILESYSTEM route through lege-hostd is not built: no org.legeos.Host.* fd-passing surface is added, and lege-filed acquires no capability.

**Context.** Recursive inotify cannot cover the reference machine — 189,089 directories after the index's skip policy against a 125,037 WatchBudget — so fanotify's FAN_MARK_FILESYSTEM, one mark per filesystem, was the obvious candidate. Two variants were measured against InotifySource on arm time, kernel and userspace memory, throughput, event fidelity, rename correctness, merging and queue overflow (@legeos.observation.unprivileged-fanotify-costs-more-per-directory-than-inotify), and the Btrfs question was answered from the kernel source with the neighbouring branch reproduced on this host (@legeos.observation.fanotify-cannot-span-btrfs-subvolumes). The unprivileged variant is one mark per directory for 6.4% more headroom, 2.5x the arm time and about twice the memory; the privileged variant returns EXDEV on every subvolume in distro/deploy/layout.toml, and a single group cannot even hold inode marks on two subvolumes.

**Consequences.** The watch-count problem is not solved by changing backend. It is solved by watching fewer directories (coverage tiers) and by treating a dormant, unwatched root as an honest state rather than a failure, which is where the effort belongs. The open question about routing a privileged fd to the per-user daemon stays open for the Btrfs-delta backend but is moot for fanotify: a passed fd carries the events without the privilege to interpret them — open_by_handle_at is EPERM for lege-filed, so the receiving daemon still needs a per-directory handle-to-path map — and it would hand a per-user daemon a view of every file on the filesystem that polkit cannot narrow after the fact. If the kernel ever grants FAN_MARK_FILESYSTEM on a Btrfs subvolume, or LegeOS abandons subvolumes, revisit from docs/measurements/fanotify-2026-09-04.md rather than from scratch.

## legeos.decision.live-iso-runs-the-provisioner

### Revision 1 — The installation medium is a LegeOS live ISO that runs the provisioner; mkosi stays the VM image

`proposed` · `@legeos.decision.live-iso-runs-the-provisioner/1` · scope `path "distro/iso/**"`, `path "distro/seeds/**"`, `path "installer/**"` · topic `installation-medium`

Developer Edition 0.1 installs from a UEFI-only live ISO built by distro/iso/build.sh: mmdebstrap from the seeds plus one build set, casper, Canonical's signed shim and removable-media GRUB copied out of the rootfs, xorriso. The live session is the LegeOS session; installing is running `legeos-install` (installer/provision.sh, shipped by legeos-cli) with --free-space or --esp/--root from a terminal, reading the plan, and adding --apply. The medium carries the build set at /legeos/devrepo, so installing needs no LegeOS network archive. mkosi remains the dev/VM disk image (ADR-0006) and is not the medium; live-build and ubuntu-image are not used because each would be a second package list.

**Context.** The reference laptop has no disk to zap, a 100 MiB ESP and a 55.9 GiB free tail; a provisioner that runs from a working Linux userspace needs a medium that is not Lubuntu before Lubuntu can go. The seeds, the layout declaration and the provisioner already existed; only a way to boot them did not.

**Consequences.** One package list drives the image, the metapackages and the medium. The live-only autologin and passwordless sudo exist only in distro/iso/live/customize.sh and are never packaged. A graphical installer remains a product decision for a release with users who did not build it. The Secure-Boot chain of the medium is proven by tests/integration/iso-qemu.sh under OVMF before any USB stick reaches the laptop.

## legeos.decision.mkosi-images

### Revision 1 — D7/ADR-0006 — mkosi builds the dev/CI/VM disk image (ESP + btrfs subvolumes); the installer ISO is a later stage

`active` · `@legeos.decision.mkosi-images/1` · scope `path "distro/image/**"`, `path "distro/iso/**"`, `path "distro/seeds/**"`

distro/image/mkosi.conf: Distribution=ubuntu Release=resolute Repositories=main,universe,restricted Format=disk Bootable=yes Bootloader=systemd-boot UnifiedKernelImages=no ToolsTree=default, mkosi.repart/ with ESP + btrfs subvolumes, packages composed from distro/seeds/*.seed by compose.sh. mkosi has no ISO output; the installer ISO comes later via ubuntu-image classic or live-build from the same seeds.

**Context.** Native Ubuntu support, UKI/signed systemd-boot options and systemd-repart give a straight path to snapshot/A-B deployments; the host currently lacks mkosi (apt install mkosi on 26.04).

**Consequences.** One declarative image definition, `mkosi vm` for tests; image build itself is out of scope for M0.

## legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands

### Revision 9 — The bar is a switcher of icons, not a row of window buttons: no Home chip, no titles, a hover row of window previews, and a reveal that needs a resting pointer

`active` · `@legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands/9` · scope `path "compositor/templar-comp/**"`, `path "crates/templar-window/**"`, `path "interfaces/wayland/**"`, `path "shell/templar-shell/**"` · topic `bottom-bar`

A single shell-drawn bottom bar, a content-width island at the bottom-left: the taskbar at the left (LegeOS window groups first, one entry each in the group accent; then one entry per open application, parked windows included and dimmed; a multi-window entry wears a count; hovering an entry after a dwell opens a row above the bar showing its windows, a grace period closes it, a click activates), then the machine cluster at the island's right end (account chip wearing the account's name, clock, network indicator, Settings; each does one named thing on one click, dimmed and inert when its thing is not installed; charge, volume and backlight are the first line of the account popover).

Every taskbar entry is one square cell wearing its application's icon, active or not. It never widens and it never prints a window title: the window wears its own name on its own tag, so a copy of that name on the bar is the duplicate inventory this desktop's redundancy rule forbids, and a row of labelled window buttons is the one thing that makes a desktop read as Windows. Names live on the hover row, beside the application's other windows.

The hover row is a strip of the windows themselves, not a list of their names: each item is a capture of that window over the standard capture protocols (the same cache Home's session tiles read, keyed by `field_model::session_identifier`) with its title under it, and the application's icon in its place until the first frame arrives or when previews are turned off. The row is the only thing that asks for a capture while a window covers Home, and it asks only for the windows it is showing and only while it is open. An item is 132 logical pixels wide where the name-only item was 220, because the surface is a content-width island and the row shares its width rather than the screen's; the band is 104 tall rather than 40, which is what a picture needs and is spent only while the pointer rests on a chip.

There is no Home chip. A Home button at the bottom-left reads as a Start menu, and Home is already what is behind everything: `home.reveal` keeps Super and the Field's own context menu, and the bar belongs to the machine, not to Home.

The bar reserves NO exclusive zone: it claims set_exclusive_zone(bottom, 0), which keeps it bottom-anchored and reserves nothing, so windows use the whole output and a maximized window wears its own tags (its controls are never duplicated on the bar). Presence is by what is under it: over Home, or with no unshelved non-fullscreen window meeting its strip, it is visible at full height; when a window is under its strip it collapses to a thin hint (a ^ on the bar's ground at the very bottom of the output). A pointer that comes to REST on the hint reveals the whole bar; being merely present on the strip does not, because a pointer crossing the bottom edge on its way elsewhere was opening the bar at inopportune times. The pointer leaving collapses it again after the same short dwell, closing any open row or popover. In fullscreen it is absent: a visible fullscreen window stacks above the shell overlay on its output, there is no bottom-edge peek, and Alt+Tab is the switch route. Window management remains on the window's tag and in the switcher; a separate popup manager is deferred (see @legeos.work.window-manager-popup-and-functional-edge-tabs).

**Context.** The user's hands-on runs showed a mouse-only user had no persistent route between windows because Home is momentary and Alt+Tab is keyboard. A reserved row wastes space; an unreserved row overlays the window. The user's answer (2026-09-08, from their cosmic fork) is presence by need: visible where nothing is under it, a hint and a mouseover elsewhere, and a hide as easy as the reveal. After deploying rev 5 the user's verdict was that the bar "looks the same ... except with more text in the buttons", "is not supposed to look windowsesqe", "has a redundant home button" and "popups up at inopportune times". Rev 6 answers those three: the 220-pixel active cell with the window's title, the 80-pixel Home chip, and a 120 ms dwell that any low pointer satisfied. The reference is the user's own cosmic-applets fork (local/dock-window-grouping: "drop taskbar mode, leave the hover switcher as the only window UI"), packed under .agent/scratch/packs/. The machine cluster keeps its labels: those are functional information about the machine, not a duplicate of anything, and stripping them would be the generic minimalism the user rejects.

**Consequences.** Compositor: unchanged from rev 5. Shell: HOME_WIDTH and ACTIVE_WIDTH are gone with the chip and the title they sized; every cell is CELL wide; HINT_OPEN_MS rises from 120 ms to 350 ms and the dwell restarts whenever the pointer moves more than HINT_REST_SLOP. The taskbar reclaims about 300 pixels. Reaching Home by pointer while a window covers the screen is now only the Field's context menu, which the covering window hides — Super is the practical route, and a non-Windows pointer route (a hot corner, or a gesture) is open. Needs no logout: the shell hot-swaps.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands/8`

The taskbar reclaims about 300 pixels. Reaching Home by pointer while a window covers the screen is now only the Field's context menu, which the covering window hides — Super is the practical route, and a non-Windows pointer route (a hot corner, or a gesture) is open. ### Revision 7 — The bar is a switcher of icons, not a row of window buttons: no Home chip, no titles, a hover row of window previews, and a reveal that needs a resting pointer

`superseded` · `@legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands/7` · scope `path "compositor/lege-comp/**"`, `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "interfaces/wayland/**"`, `path "shell/lege-shell/**"` · topic `bottom-bar`

A single shell-drawn bottom bar, a content-width island at the bottom-left: the taskbar at the left (LegeOS window groups first, one entry each in the group accent; then one entry per open application, parked windows included and dimmed; a multi-window entry wears a count; hovering an entry after a dwell opens a row above the bar showing its windows, a grace period closes it, a click activates), then the machine cluster at the island's right end (account chip wearing the account's name, clock, network indicator, Settings; each does one named thing on one click, dimmed and inert when its thing is not installed; charge, volume and backlight are the first line of the account popover).

Every taskbar entry is one square cell wearing its application's icon, active or not. It never widens and it never prints a window title: the window wears its own name on its own tag, so a copy of that name on the bar is the duplicate inventory this desktop's redundancy rule forbids, and a row of labelled window buttons is the one thing that makes a desktop read as Windows. Names live on the hover row, beside the application's other windows.

The hover row is a strip of the windows themselves, not a list of their names: each item is a capture of that window over the standard capture protocols (the same cache Home's session tiles read, keyed by `field_model::session_identifier`) with its title under it, and the application's icon in its place until the first frame arrives or when previews are turned off. The row is the only thing that asks for a capture while a window covers Home, and it asks only for the windows it is showing and only while it is open. An item is 132 logical pixels wide where the name-only item was 220, because the surface is a content-width island and the row shares its width rather than the screen's; the band is 104 tall rather than 40, which is what a picture needs and is spent only while the pointer rests on a chip.

There is no Home chip. A Home button at the bottom-left reads as a Start menu, and Home is already what is behind everything: `home.reveal` keeps Super and the Field's own context menu, and the bar belongs to the machine, not to Home.

The bar reserves NO exclusive zone: it claims set_exclusive_zone(bottom, 0), which keeps it bottom-anchored and reserves nothing, so windows use the whole output and a maximized window wears its own tags (its controls are never duplicated on the bar). Presence is by what is under it: over Home, or with no unshelved non-fullscreen window meeting its strip, it is visible at full height; when a window is under its strip it collapses to a thin hint (a ^ on the bar's ground at the very bottom of the output). A pointer that comes to REST on the hint reveals the whole bar; being merely present on the strip does not, because a pointer crossing the bottom edge on its way elsewhere was opening the bar at inopportune times. The pointer leaving collapses it again after the same short dwell, closing any open row or popover. Window management remains on the window's tag and in the switcher; a separate popup manager is deferred (see @legeos.work.window-manager-popup-and-functional-edge-tabs).

**Context.** The user's hands-on runs showed a mouse-only user had no persistent route between windows because Home is momentary and Alt+Tab is keyboard. A reserved row wastes space; an unreserved row overlays the window. The user's answer (2026-09-08, from their cosmic fork) is presence by need: visible where nothing is under it, a hint and a mouseover elsewhere, and a hide as easy as the reveal. After deploying rev 5 the user's verdict was that the bar "looks the same ... except with more text in the buttons", "is not supposed to look windowsesqe", "has a redundant home button" and "popups up at inopportune times". Rev 6 answers those three: the 220-pixel active cell with the window's title, the 80-pixel Home chip, and a 120 ms dwell that any low pointer satisfied. The reference is the user's own cosmic-applets fork (local/dock-window-grouping: "drop taskbar mode, leave the hover switcher as the only window UI"), packed under .agent/scratch/packs/. The machine cluster keeps its labels: those are functional information about the machine, not a duplicate of anything, and stripping them would be the generic minimalism the user rejects.

**Consequences.** Compositor: unchanged from rev 5. Shell: HOME_WIDTH and ACTIVE_WIDTH are gone with the chip and the title they sized; every cell is CELL wide; HINT_OPEN_MS rises from 120 ms to 350 ms and the dwell restarts whenever the pointer moves more than HINT_REST_SLOP. The taskbar reclaims about 300 pixels. Reaching Home by pointer while a window covers the screen is now only the Field's context menu, which the covering window hides — Super is the practical route, and a non-Windows pointer route (a hot corner, or a gesture) is open. Needs no logout: the shell hot-swaps.

### Revision 5 — Window tags and shell controls; the bar reserves nothing, shows over Home, collapses to a hint under windows, and is absent in fullscreen

`superseded` · `@legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands/5` · scope `path "compositor/lege-comp/**"`, `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "interfaces/wayland/**"`, `path "shell/lege-shell/**"` · topic `bottom-bar`

A single shell-drawn bottom bar, the output's full width: Home chip at the left, then the taskbar (LegeOS window groups first, one entry each in the group accent; then one entry per open application, parked windows included and dimmed; a multi-window entry wears a count; hovering an entry after a dwell opens a row above the bar listing its windows, a grace period closes it, a click activates), then the machine cluster at the right end (account chip wearing the account's name, clock, network indicator, Settings; each does one named thing on one click, dimmed and inert when its thing is not installed; charge, volume and backlight are the first line of the account popover). The bar reserves NO exclusive zone: it claims set_exclusive_zone(bottom, 0), which keeps it bottom-anchored and reserves nothing, so windows use the whole output and a maximized window wears its own tags (its controls are never duplicated on the bar). Presence is by what is under it: over Home, or with no unshelved non-fullscreen window meeting its strip, it is visible at full height; when a window is under its strip it collapses to a thin hint (a ^ on the bar's ground at the very bottom of the output), a pointer resting on the hint reveals the whole bar, and the pointer leaving it collapses it again after the same short dwell, closing any open row or popover. In fullscreen it is absent: a visible fullscreen window stacks above the shell overlay on its output, there is no bottom-edge peek, and Alt+Tab is the switch route. A reserved row wastes space; an unreserved row overlays the window. The user's answer (2026-09-08, from their cosmic fork) is presence by need: visible where nothing is under it, a hint and a mouseover elsewhere, and a hide as easy as the reveal. The reviewer's redundancy principle (rev 3/4: a window's name and controls belong to the window) is kept; their replacement of the bar by a popup is not — the bar is the switcher.

**Consequences.** Compositor: a zero-size zone claim anchors without reserving (lege-shell-v1 prose clarified, no signature change); the fullscreen peek of campaign 3 is deleted; has_frame gives maximized windows their tags because no bottom zone is claimed. Shell: the bar's maximized-window controls go; covered/hint/revealed presence with two short dwells; the Home field still ends above the bar. Needs one logout. Rev 4's peek-on-hardware acceptance is retired.

### Revision 4 — Window tags and shell controls; fullscreen hides the bar and window management is explicitly summoned

`superseded` · `@legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands/4` · scope `path "compositor/lege-comp/**"`, `path "crates/lege-window/**"`, `path "interfaces/wayland/**"`, `path "shell/lege-shell/**"` · topic `bottom-bar`

Outside a fullscreen presentation, a single shell-drawn bottom bar is visible over application windows and on Home, and reserves an Edge::Bottom exclusive zone. It is the output's full width: Home chip at the left (a pointer route to the Home Field, so a bare Super tap is not the only one), then the taskbar, then the machine cluster at the right end. Taskbar: LegeOS window groups first (one entry each in the group accent), then one entry per open application (a single-window application is that window), parked windows included and dimmed — Home places no tile for a running or parked window, so the bar is the only place one exists, and a click on a parked entry unshelves it before activating it. Hovering an entry after a dwell opens a second row above the bar listing its windows, a grace period closes it, a click activates. Machine cluster, right to left: an account chip wearing the account's own name, the clock, the network indicator and a Settings chip. Every one of the four does one named thing on one click — the account chip opens its popover; the clock opens the installed calendar (`clock.open-calendar`); the network indicator opens whichever application fills the `network-status-ui` provider role, with `--popup`; the Settings chip opens Settings — and a chip whose thing is not installed is drawn dimmed and takes no click rather than looking live and doing nothing. There is no separate readings chip: charge, volume and backlight are the first line of the account popover, which also holds the volume and brightness controls and the session actions (lock, suspend, log out, restart, shut down; the three that end the session wear an ellipsis, take a second click, and read "Click again to log out" while armed). That popover is the only pointer route to the session and machine actions now that Home carries no Session widget; Settings has left it for a chip of its own, because an action offered in two places is one a person has to look for twice. Bottom-right of all of it: park, maximize and close for the activated window when it is maximized. The compositor-drawn title band above every window is retired: a non-maximized window carries compositor-drawn tags on its bottom edge, a name tag bottom-left (title, group accent stripe; the grab-to-move and group-drop affordance) and contiguous control tags bottom-right; a maximized window on an output with a bottom exclusive zone draws no tags, and draws them again whenever no such zone is claimed, so controls never vanish when the shell is dead. The corner resize grip is removed; resize is the margin ring outside every edge and corner. The user's planning direction on 2026-09-08 replaces the fullscreen peek clause: while a fullscreen application is being presented on an output, the taskbar is not shown, including on hover, edge dwell, or pointer contact. It must not remain visibly composited underneath a translucent fullscreen client. Fullscreen occupies the complete logical output and preserves the preceding geometry and mode for restoration. Window management is to be an explicitly summoned popup using adapted cosmic-applets code; opening that manager does not reveal the bar. Ordinary window tags and their compact functional design language are retained. The detailed popup behavior, invocation defaults, non-fullscreen edge composition, and gradual redundancy removals are proposals under @legeos.work.window-manager-popup-and-functional-edge-tabs; this revision does not adopt those recommendations wholesale or authorize implementation.

**Context.** The user's hands-on runs showed a disconnect between Home and open windows: a mouse-only user had no persistent route between windows because Home is momentary and Alt+Tab is keyboard, and a window's controls sat at the top while the user's attention and the proposed taskbar sit at the bottom. The user first proposed moving the band to the bottom with a Windows 3.1 style window-list box, then replaced that with the shared bar: 'every open window shares the bar and the bar does double duty as a taskbar'. The hover-row behaviour is ported from cosmic-app-list (GPL-3, libcosmic); behaviour only, no code copied into this AGPL-3 repository. The 2026-09-08 run added the rest: docs/garden/garden.md's division of labour — Home deals with your things, the bar deals with the machine — made the scattered Session/Settings/sound/battery widgets one cluster; 'full screen mode should be genuinely full screen with taskbar mouseover' and 'doing away with the Super button as only way to get to home screen' are the fullscreen, peek and Home-chip clauses. The cluster composition changed again the same day, from the user's report on the installed session: 'the bottom right buttons arent clickable. network should open nm-tray-2. there should be no separate power/battery bar. need that space for a full OS settings button that opens into all settings areas. similarly date/time should open. and i dont know what the furthest bottom right button does and i dont want to click it in case it will log me out.' Two of the four chips had no click handler at all, the readings chip was a number nobody could go anywhere from, and the account chip was an unlabelled mark.

**Consequences.** Planning-only revision from the user's explicit request. The current implementation still contains bottom-edge peek and must not be represented as satisfying this new behavior. The old peek-on-hardware acceptance is retired by the successor work. Fullscreen visibility and popup stacking need distinct policies so invoking the manager cannot raise the machine cluster or other ordinary shell chrome. The cluster clause is implemented by @legeos.work.bar-cluster-clickable-20260908. Its rule that a chip with nothing behind it is dimmed rather than inert-looking has a cost the composition has to carry: `gsimplecal` and `legeos-nm-tray` are now part of the desktop set, and on a machine without them two of the four chips are visibly unavailable. That is the intended failure mode, not a regression.

**supersedes** `@legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands/3` · **superseded by** `@legeos.decision.one-persistent-bottom-bar-tags-not-bands/5`
